title: Secure VM Foundation — v3
objective: Sol orchestrates; Luna investigates and implements. Current phase ONLY: establish evidence, then smallest clean-checkout → Dev VM → Little Mester responds → Docker container executes milestone. User confirms /workspace is the fresh feat/vm-approach-3 checkout from main, permits local edits/commits here, and reserves pushes to the end user. Base SHA fc863532b18e21aabd8cb87f4266eed9afafd89c (HEAD and cached origin/main observed equal); live remote freshness cannot be independently checked because GitHub DNS failed. This clarification supersedes the earlier separate-worktree blocker; do not move branches or disturb the running VM. Preserve feat/vm-approach and feat/vm-approach-2 and all unrelated work. No implementation until investigation evidence is reviewed by Sol.

acceptance_criteria.text: LOCKED D1–D3: trusted Host Launcher alone creates/destroys VMs; each VM accesses exclusively its assigned workspace; host-side MCP and CLI are thin adapters over one core security/authorisation library.

LOCKED D4–D6: ordinary agents cannot create VMs; host-granted Dev self-test capability disabled by default, one disposable Test VM maximum, Test VMs cannot recurse; host establishes caller identity/permissions, never agent parameters or guest-editable configuration; prefer host-created siblings, no nested virtualisation unless demonstrated necessary.

LOCKED D7–D10: one working provider initially, no local-model optimisation; security controls outside agent-editable workspaces; first milestone proves clean checkout launches Dev VM, Little Mester responds and guest Docker runs a container; old branches remain untouched until explicit cleanup approval.

Target workflow retained without planning later implementation: isolated single-workspace Dev VM supports normal Docker work; explicitly authorised disposable Test VM tests a fresh snapshot of actual changes; bounded iterations; tested cohesive commits; only suggest Dev VM refresh onto verified branch, NEVER refresh automatically.

Immediate child investigation compares both branches by capability with paths and concrete evidence, no implementation or broad commit archaeology; Sol reviews evidence before defining one implementation ticket. No wholesale merges/blind cherry-picks; reuse proven cohesive portions, simplify without weakening security.

Implementation ticket must specify objective, exact files, existing code to reuse, security constraints, ordered instructions, exact evidence-backed test commands and expected results, acceptance criteria and commit checkpoint. Unknown commands are discovered, not invented. Luna owns implementation; Sol reviews actual changes and acceptance evidence and decides completion.

Execution: only one active v3 implementation task; tickets only for current milestone; no sprawling plans/frameworks; document → test → code → commit; tests/evidence before cohesive commits; stop after two identical failures without new evidence; host actions NEEDS_HUMAN; source changes do not change running runtime; never agent-controlled privilege grants. No resets, discards, deletion, force pushes or automatic VM replacement. End user alone pushes, merges, approves scope/security/architecture expansion or deletes work.

External review contract: every user-facing progress report, completed task, milestone, blocker, change/approval request and PR boundary ends with a compact YAML handoff packet; persist the same packet in relevant ticket through MCP. ChatGPT/Claude are independent advisory reviewers, not authorities. Extract concrete feedback, check against requirements/evidence, apply justified in-scope changes; otherwise request user approval with CHANGE_REQUEST, without restarting planning. No expensive model solely for report rewriting.
